clue.text: Study backward boy and cause outrage

parts.note: to scan something is to study or examine it closely

indicators.note: backward tells us the word for boy is to be read from right to left

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A rebellious boy who studies in reverse provokes public indignation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' applies only to the boy, not to Study. 'and cause' is link: a public furore is what the boy causes, so the definition is the noun outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: A public furore over shocking conduct can be called either an outrage or a scandal; the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Drink to worker in the Seychelles

indicators.note: in places the worker inside the abbreviation for the island nation

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle registration code for the Seychelles
a hand is a manual worker, as in a farm hand

explanation.surface: A toast raised to a labourer out in the Indian Ocean islands.
explanation.walkthrough: A SHANDY is a British pub drink of beer mixed with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer topped up with lemonade is a long refreshing beverage, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Handsome youth in trouble over recurrent offence

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble, as in much ado about nothing

indicators.note: recurrent, read as running back, says the word for offence is turned round

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence

explanation.surface: A good-looking young man gets into bother for repeatedly breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurrent' is read as running back, the reversal signal; 'over' works because this is a down entry, with the trouble word written above. 'in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, his name became a byword for any strikingly handsome young man.

clue.text: Trifle served by foolish, dunderheaded friend

parts.note: dilly is informal (chiefly Australian) for silly or foolish

indicators.note: headed asks for just the leading letter of the word dunder that it is joined to

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A dessert dished up by a silly, thick-headed companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' looks like the pudding but is the verb, to waste time. 'dunderheaded' splits as dunder plus headed: the head of dunder is D. 'served by' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle is to dawdle or idle about, just as to dilly-dally is to waste time.

clue.text: Scowl if it's reduced in value

definitions.meaning: to frown or look sullen and threatening, also spelt lour
brought down to a smaller amount, as prices are cut

explanation.surface: Someone frowns at learning their savings have shrunk.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves both as a verb meaning to frown darkly and as the comparative of low, describing something cut in value.

clue.text: Nobleman and king harboured by French resistance

indicators.note: harboured by means the king is sheltered inside the resistance word

parts.note: the Maquis were the French Resistance fighters of the Second World War
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An aristocrat and a monarch are hidden by wartime French partisans.
explanation.walkthrough: The Maquis were rural guerrilla bands of the French Resistance in WWII.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank of the peerage between duke and count, so its holder is a titled aristocrat.

clue.text: Ill-treat fellow with a title

parts.note: a fellow is a man
a handle is informal for a person's title or name

explanation.surface: A man who has just acquired a title is treated roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' is slang for a title, as in having a handle to one's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle someone roughly or with force is to abuse or ill-treat them.

clue.text: Overcharge when in a hurry

definitions.meaning: informal sense of charging a customer far too much

explanation.surface: A tradesman fleeces a customer who has no time to argue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when in a' links the two senses: the first is the slangy British verb for fleecing someone on price.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for fleecing a customer on price and also means haste or a sudden dash.

clue.text: Woman takes commodities in all innocence

parts.note: Una is a woman's name
wares are goods or commodities for sale

explanation.surface: A naive woman accepts goods without suspecting anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is only a link word here, not a container signal; Una is a traditional woman's name, as in Spenser's Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught off guard, without knowing or intending, a person acts innocently and without awareness.

clue.text: Pay Swede to design a racetrack

indicators.note: to design means to plan or lay out, so the letters are rearranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian is hired to lay out a new circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to design' rearranges PAYSWEDE into SPEEDWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorcycle racing takes place on an oval circuit, a track built for racing.

clue.text: A ring of islands

parts.note: to toll a bell is to ring it

explanation.surface: A plain description of a circle of coral islets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a circle but in the wordplay is the bell sense, TOLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A coral reef enclosing a lagoon forms a circular chain of islets.

clue.text: Became distraught when left redundant

definitions.meaning: British slang for becoming furious or frantic
turned out to be surplus to requirements

explanation.surface: A worker lost the plot on being laid off.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang for flying into a rage, and literally means went unused.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means lost one's temper, and taken literally says a thing became a spare, surplus item.

clue.text: Char needs money to make a living

parts.note: a char or daily is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman must earn enough to get by.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'char' (charwoman) and a 'daily' are both old British words for a cleaner; 'needs' and 'to make a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from the Lord's Prayer means the food or earnings needed to live, one's livelihood.

clue.text: Reportedly prohibited a group of players

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for prohibited is heard rather than seen

parts.note: banned means prohibited

explanation.surface: Rumour says a group of musicians has been barred.
explanation.walkthrough: BANNED and BAND sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians who play together form a band.

clue.text: TT champion engineered decisive moment in court

indicators.note: engineered means contrived or reconstructed, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A motorcycle racer rigs the outcome of a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Isle of Man TT motorcycle race; 'engineered' rearranges TTCHAMPION. 'court' is a tennis court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, the point that would win the whole contest for one player is a deciding moment.

clue.text: Its shots are unforeseen

parts.note: shots sound like gunfire or sports attempts, but these are filmed scenes that the people in them do not see coming

explanation.surface: A remark about surprise attacks or unexpected goals.
explanation.walkthrough: A hidden-camera TV show filmed people's reactions to staged pranks without their knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A television show filming unwitting people with a concealed lens, so its footage takes them by surprise.

clue.text: Way to get in a nail?

parts.note: a drive is a road or way
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A question about how to hammer a nail into wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The question looks like carpentry, but 'nail' is the verb to make a point stick; the question mark flags this. 'to get' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail an argument is to press it with force until it is fully understood.

clue.text: Huge caper following pop-group show

indicators.note: following places the caper word after the show

parts.note: a gig is a live performance by a pop group
an antic is a playful caper or prank

explanation.surface: A massive stunt is staged after a band's concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the caper after the show; a gig is the usual word for a live set by a band.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enormous or colossal in size is huge.

clue.text: Racer receives capital attention endlessly

parts.note: stock is capital, the funds invested in a business

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter from the word for attention

parts.note: care is close attention

explanation.surface: A competitor collects money and focus without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims CARE to CAR. 'receives' is link. Stock car racing uses modified ordinary cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A modified production car driven in races, so it is a vehicle that competes.

clue.text: Information-gathering requires brainpower

definitions.meaning: the work of secret services in collecting information about enemies

explanation.surface: Spying on others needs a sharp mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both espionage, the gathering of secret information, and mental capacity or cleverness.

clue.text: Many go as result of split

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, so many
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Lots of people leave once there has been a split.
explanation.walkthrough: Using C for 'many' (the Roman numeral 100) is a crossword convention. 'as result of' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to chop or split something apart, as with a cleaver.

clue.text: Roman coin mailed by agreement

parts.note: the as was a bronze coin of ancient Rome
sent means mailed

explanation.surface: An ancient coin is posted by mutual consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is link; the as was a basic copper coin of the Roman Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Consent or approval given to a proposal is agreement.

clue.text: Cardinal seen in a Catholic hospital

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A senior churchman spotted at a Catholic infirmary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman, but is the adjective meaning chief or principal. 'seen in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, cardinal means principal or chief, as does arch in arch-enemy.

clue.text: Sole import produced in new York, say

indicators.note: produced means made or put together, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A flatfish brought in through the Big Apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like the fish; 'produced' rearranges SOLEIMPORT. 'in' is link and 'say' marks the city as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge, important city, of which the largest US city is an example.

clue.text: Assign to adjudicator with little demur

parts.note: a ref (referee) is an adjudicator
er is a small sound of hesitation or mild objection

explanation.surface: Pass a matter to an umpire with a slight objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'with' are link words; ER is the hesitant noise made when mildly objecting.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on or attribute a matter to someone is to assign it to them.

clue.text: She came from Denver ages ago

indicators.note: came from says the name is drawn out of the letters of Denver ages

explanation.surface: A woman arrived from a Colorado city long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ago' is link that completes the surface; VERA runs across 'DenVER Ages'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it can stand for any woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Censured for having filled in the boxes

definitions.meaning: having marked boxes on a form with check marks

explanation.surface: Someone was reprimanded for completing a form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the senses: the first is British slang for scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for reprimanded, and literally having marked boxes with checks.

clue.text: Independent redhead consumed with anger

indicators.note: head asks for only the leading letter of the word red that it is joined to

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A self-reliant redhead burns with fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' splits as red plus head: the head of red is R.
explanation.definitionFit: To be consumed with anger is to be furious or enraged.

clue.text: Slaughter harridan in custody

indicators.note: in places the harridan inside the custody word

parts.note: care is custody, as in being taken into care
a nag is a scolding woman or harridan

explanation.surface: An old scold is held after a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slaughter' could be a verb, but the definition is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloody killing of many people is slaughter or butchery.

clue.text: Shout again and turn tail

definitions.meaning: to buy another round of drinks, from the Australian slang shout meaning to treat

explanation.surface: A man calls out once more and then runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shout' is slang (Australian and British) for buying a round; read as re-treat, it means stand treat again.
explanation.definitionFit: The word read as re-treat means treat again, buying another round; and it also means to withdraw or flee.
